subject.title: feat(discord): add canvas-first Discord Activities support

question: Should Discord Activity support proceed as a Canvas-plugin-owned feature with a fail-closed Activity auth model, or should this PR be paused in favor of a different owner/security design?
rationale: The unresolved blockers cross plugin ownership, Gateway authorization, token transport, public Canvas exposure, and SDK supply chain, so automation can identify defects but should not choose the permanent Activity security boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
options.body: Move the Activity host/config bridge into extensions/canvas and extensions/discord, require credentialed Activity access, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and ask for live Discord proof before merge.

options.title: Approve a different Activity boundary
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept a different public Activity auth design, but the credential path and exposure tradeoff should be explicit before merge.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Keep the branch as design context and restart from a smaller branch if the current conflicts and security changes are too costly to repair.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
recommendation.body: Move the Activity host/config bridge into extensions/canvas and extensions/discord, require credentialed Activity access, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and ask for live Discord proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the Canvas plugin route/config boundary introduced by PR 78558.
